deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). A candidate system of pseudolines (D_i)_{i∈I} in a closed surface X is given combinatorially by three pieces of data:
- a graph K with vertex set S and edge set A;
- for each vertex s, the set I_s of pseudolines through s, with ν_s = d_s = card I_s;
- a map structure (rotation system) at s, i.e. a cyclic permutation vec ξ_s (ρ) of the set of oriented lines through s.
Condition (22) on the previous page requires ρ^{ν_s}(vec D) = −vec D: going halfway round the vertex reverses each line. Euler–Poincaré, c0 − c1 + c2 = 1, then forces X to be the projective plane. Grothendieck is now constructing and constraining the admissible local rotations vec ξ_s.

Step 1, map (25). For a vertex s and a pseudoline Δ not passing through s, define φ_{s,Δ}: I_s → S_Δ (the set of vertices of K lying on Δ) by D_i ∩ Δ = {φ(D_i)}.
- φ is well defined because two distinct pseudolines meet in exactly one point.
- φ is injective because two distinct lines through s already meet at s, so they cannot also meet on Δ.

Step 2, induced polygon structure. Δ is a pseudoline, topologically a circle, so its vertex set S_Δ carries a polygon (dihedral) structure: a cyclic order up to reversal. Pulling back along φ gives a polygon structure ξ#_{s,Δ} on I_s.

Step 3, axiom (A1). ξ#_{s,Δ} should not depend on the choice of Δ ∈ I∖I_s; the common value is called ξ#_s. In a genuine arrangement this holds: the pencil of pseudolines through s sweeps every other pseudoline in the same cyclic order. This is the familiar 'local sequence' consistency. The margin says it is to be proved when the configuration actually comes from a pseudoline system in X, and that the condition has content only for larger d_s.

Step 4, compatibility (26)–(27). Let vec I_s → I_s be the 2:1 map that forgets orientation. Condition (27): the rotation vec u ∈ vec ξ_s, viewed as a permutation of vec I_s, must descend to a permutation u of I_s, and u must be one of the two cyclic orders forming the polygon structure ξ'_s (= ξ#_s).

Step 5, count. Grothendieck says this sharply restricts the choice: 2^{d_s−1} possibilities, worked out on the next page.
- Fix an orientation u0 of the polygon I_s.
- Lifting u0 to the double cover means choosing, for each i, a bijection between the orientation fibre of D_i and that of D_{u0(i)}: 2^{ν} choices (signed lifts).
- The lift must be a single 2ν-cycle. Its ν-th power acts on each fibre by the product of the signs, so it is transitive exactly when that product is −1. This halves the count to 2^{ν−1}.
- Transitivity also gives ρ^ν = antipode automatically, so the lifts are consistent with (22).

Purpose. This step builds a local-to-global reconstruction theorem: when do combinatorial data (graph plus local rotations) come from an arrangement of pseudolines in P^2?
errors: The marginal note seems to say (A1) is non-trivial already for d_s ≥ 3. With 'structure polygonale' defined (eq. (24)) as a pair of mutually opposite cyclic orders, a 3-element set carries exactly one such structure. So (A1) only has content for d_s ≥ 4, unless 'ordre circulaire' is meant oriented or the reading of the margin is wrong.

(A1) is stated as an axiom; the margin records that its necessity, i.e. that it holds when the data come from an actual pseudoline system, is still to be proved. It is a gap on the page, though the fact is standard and easy.

The count 2^{d_s−1} is stated for lifts compatible with a fixed orientation u0. Counting both orientations of the polygon would give 2^{d_s}. This is a minor bookkeeping ambiguity, resolved on the next page.

ideas.what: Map φ_{s,Δ}: lines through a vertex s → vertices on a line Δ not through s; it is injective, and pulls back Δ's cyclic order to the pencil at s
ideas.modern_name: Pencil/central projection in pseudoline arrangements; local sequences of crossings

ideas.what: Axiom (A1): the cyclic order of the pencil at s is the same whichever line Δ it is read on
ideas.modern_name: Consistency of local sequences / pseudoline-arrangement axioms (cf. oriented matroid chirotope axioms of rank 3)

ideas.what: Lifting a polygon (dihedral) structure on the lines through s to a rotation of the 2ν half-lines (oriented lines) via the double cover; count 2^{ν−1} via the product-of-signs condition for a single 2ν-cycle
ideas.modern_name: Signed cyclic permutations / lifts to the orientation double cover; rotation systems of combinatorial maps (antipodal condition)

ideas.what: Overall programme: characterising pseudoline arrangements in P^2 by combinatorial map data plus an Euler characteristic condition
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial characterisation of (simple and non-simple) pseudoline arrangements; rank-3 oriented matroids
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to around Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in the context of 'tame topology'/combinatorial geometry; unsure

missed.claim: This is an independent, early-1980s reconstruction by Grothendieck of the local–global axiomatics of pseudoline arrangements, phrased in terms of maps (cartes) and polygon structures rather than oriented matroids. On this page the content is standard (pencil order consistency, signed lifts). It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.
missed.quote: (A1) ξ#_{s,Δ} est indépendante des choix de Δ ∈ I ∖ I_s, soit ξ#_s.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's dessins/maps viewpoint being applied to pseudoline arrangements. This fits historical studies linking the Esquisse-era work on cartes to combinatorial geometry; no new theorem is visible here.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine but careful steps: injectivity of the projection, consistency of induced cyclic orders, and counting signed lifts (2^{ν−1}). All are standard facts in pseudoline/oriented-matroid theory. Its interest is mainly as part of Grothendieck's unpublished pseudoline project.
transcription_corrections: The cyclic-order symbols ξ/𝔷 (Gothic z) are used inconsistently between pages; on this page ξ'_s, ξ#_s and vec ξ_s refer to the same objects as 𝔷'_s, 𝔷_s on neighbouring pages.
The opening word is likely 'canonique(ment)' (an application canonique I_s → S_Δ); the item after the arrow is 'ens. S_Δ des sommets de K sur Δ'.
'd_s' on this page equals 'ν_s' (number of lines through s) on neighbouring pages.
The margin at (A1) is probably 'Condition non vide que pour d_s ≥ 3' or similar; reading uncertain.
In (27) the inserted '∈ 𝔖_{vec I_s}' indicates that vec ξ_s ⊂ 𝔖_{vec I_s} (permutations of the oriented lines), and the condition reads 'u se descend en u ∈ 𝔖_{I_s}, et on a u ∈ ξ'_s'.
'importante' in 'condition restrictive importante' is plausible; the final phrase is 'qui limite le choix : 2^{d_s−1} possibilités'.
